sanskrit: agnyagrā indrabalā ādityā ye yudho viduḥ | yudho adhi pratiṣṭhitā hotrā jaitrāya juhvati ||
english: Those Ādityas who are Agni-led and Indra-powered, who know battles — established as foremost in battle, the priests pour oblations for victory.

sanskrit: abhiyuktasya pradhane 'nu yoddhāram icchatām | havīṃṣy agre yudhyatāṃ prati gṛhṇīta juhvatām ||
english: For the one engaged in the foremost combat, desiring a warrior to follow — accept the oblations of those who fight at the vanguard, of those who pour the offering.

sanskrit: jetrā rājñā varuṇena jetrā rudreṇa keśinā | bhavena jiṣṇunā jayati parjanyena sahīyasā ||
english: He conquers by Varuṇa the victorious king, by Rudra the long-haired victor; by Bhava the triumphant he wins, and by Parjanya the exceedingly mighty.

sanskrit: astrā tāmreṇa bṛhatā- -astrā śarveṇa yudhyatā | gandharveṇa tviṣīmatā rathenāsamayodhinā ||
english: By the weapon of the great copper-hued one, by the weapon of Śarva the warrior; by the Gandharva full of fiery brilliance, on his chariot that fights without an equal.

sanskrit: sinīvāly anumatir vāhāśvā niṣaṅgiṇaḥ | jayanto 'bhi pretāmitrān sākam indreṇa medinā ||
english: Sinīvālī and Anumati, bearing swift horses, quiver-bearing — conquering, they advance against the enemies together with Indra the ally.

sanskrit: yat svapne nijagantha yad vā śepiṣe 'nṛtam | agniṣ ṭvā tasmād enaso brahmā muñcatv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: Whatever you have struck down in a dream, or whatever falsehood you have uttered — may Agni, may Brahmā release you from that transgression, from that sin.

sanskrit: yad akṣeṣu dudrohitha yad vā mitrebhyas tvam | somas tvā tasmād enaso brahmā muñcatv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: Whatever treachery you have committed at dice, or whatever you have done against friends — may Soma, may Brahmā release you from that transgression, from that sin.

sanskrit: yat kumāraḥ kumāreṣu yad vā jyāyastareṣu ca | nīviṃ yat kṛtvā śepiṣe tat kṛṇmo agadaṃ śivam ||
english: What as a youth you have uttered among youths, or what among elders; what you have spoken having made a wager — that we make auspicious and free of disease.

sanskrit: pratīcīnaphalo hi tvam apāmārga babhūvitha | sarvān mac chapathām̐ adhi varīyo yāvayā tvam ||
english: For you, O Apāmārga, have become backward-fruited; drive away from me all the curses, driving them to something broader.

sanskrit: apāmārga oṣadhīnāṃ viśvāsām eka it patiḥ | tena te mṛjma āsthitam atha tvam agadaś cara ||
english: The Apāmārga plant is truly the sole lord of all herbs; with it we wipe away what has settled upon you — now move about free of disease.

sanskrit: śatavāro anīnaśad yakṣmān rakṣāṃsi tejasā | ārohan varcasā saha maṇir durṇāmacātanaḥ ||
english: The hundred-ringed one has destroyed the wasting diseases and the demons with its brilliance; ascending with radiance, this amulet drives away those of evil name.

sanskrit: śṛṅgābhyāṃ rakṣo nudate mūlena yātudhānyaḥ | madhyena yakṣmaṃ bādhate nainaṃ pāpmāti ?tatrati ||
english: With its horns it pushes away the Rakṣas, with its root the Yātudhānīs; with its middle it repels the wasting disease — no evil passes beyond it.

sanskrit: ye yakṣmāso arbhakā mahānto ye ca śabdinaḥ | sarvān durṇāmahā maṇiḥ śatavāro anīnaśat ||
english: The wasting diseases that are small, those that are great, and those that are noisy — the hundred-ringed amulet, slayer of those of evil name, has destroyed them all.

sanskrit: śataṃ vīrān ajanayac chataṃ yakṣmān apāvapat | durṇāmnaḥ sarvān hatvā- -apa rakṣāṃsi dhūnute ||
english: It has generated a hundred heroes; it has swept away a hundred wasting diseases; having slain all those of evil name, it shakes off the demons.

sanskrit: hiraṇyaśṛṅga ṛṣabhaḥ śātavāro ayaṃ maṇiḥ | durṇāmnaḥ sarvān tṛḍhvā- -ava rakṣāṃsy akramīt ||
english: A bull with golden horns — this hundred-ringed amulet; having pierced all those of evil name, it has stepped down upon the demons.

sanskrit: śatam ahaṃ durṇāmnīnāṃ gandharvāpsarasāṃ śatam | śataṃ śvanvatīnāṃ śatavāreṇa vāraye ||
english: A hundred of those evil-named ones, a hundred Gandharvas and Apsarases, a hundred she-demons accompanied by dogs — with the hundred-ringed amulet I ward them all off.
